• Scientific name: Pseudolaguvia shawi (Hora, 1921)
  • Common name: Shaw's Bee Catfish
  • Type locality: Mahanadi R. below Darjeeling, West Bengal, India.
  • Synonyms: Glyptothorax shawi, Laguvia shawi
  • IUCN Red List: Least Concern (last assessed 2009)

• Asia: Indian waters, Sikkim State
  • Indian waters, Bengal, West Bengal, Darjeeling District
  • Indian waters, Arunachal Pradesh State
  • Indian waters, North Eastern India, Padma, Jamuna, Brahmaputra, Manas (Mou chhu)
Known to take only live food like bloodworms, frozen brine shrimp etc. Spot feeding will help in case tank mates are voracious feeders.

A peaceful species suitable for a hillstream biotope. Extreme care should be taken while choosing their tankmates as these fish are extremely poor at competing for food.

Suggested tankmates: cyprinids like Barilius and Danio and balitorine loaches like Homaloptera species.
Unreported in the aquarium. There is no breeding report.

Members of the genus Pseudolaguvia are small erethistid catfishes inhabiting hill streams and large rivers in the area bordered by the Ganges River drainage (northern India) to the west and the Sittang River drainage (east-central Myanmar) to the east. They can be distinguished from other sisorids by their small size, a combination of a thoracic adhesive apparatus with a median depression and prominent postcoracoid processes.
Records of the Indian Museum (Calcutta) v. 22 (pt 5, no. 33), pp 740, Pl. 29 (fig. 2).
